solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who backs husband against narrow-minded sort?

definitions.text: One who backs husband against narrow-minded sort?

indicators.note: against here means next to, so the following piece is set alongside

parts.note: a punter who backs a horse is a better, someone who bets
ALF is Australian slang for a boorish, narrow-minded man

explanation.surface: A wife stands by her husband in the face of some bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a spouse is the one who backs her husband. ALF is an Australian slang term for a philistine; Chambers lists it without the regional tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse, jocularly called one's better half, is the person expected to support a partner through anything.

clue.text: Uniform case finally dumped

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for case is dropped

parts.note: as in 'in any case' or 'in any event', so case means event

explanation.surface: A legal case in uniform is finally thrown out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even is regular and unvarying throughout, which is what uniform means.

clue.text: Tasteless ornamentation also in military show

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless decoration or trinkets
too means also

explanation.surface: Gaudy decoration also turns up at a military display.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British slang for tacky, worthless goods. The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous Scottish display of marching bands and drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening display of military music and marching, originally a drum signal recalling soldiers.

clue.text: Sort of trout I tucked into a brown liquid

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the single letter goes within the other letters
liquid means fluid, unfixed in form, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A trout is tucked into some brown liquid, perhaps a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown liquid' reads as gravy, but 'liquid' is the anagram signal: A BROWN rearranged gives RANBOW, and 'tucked into' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainbow trout is a common species of salmonid fish, named for its iridescent pinkish stripe.

clue.text: Hotshot getting to grips with hard hurt

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a hotshot
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A star player tackles a tough opponent and gets injured.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to suffer a dull, continuous pain, so it is a synonym for hurt as a verb.

clue.text: Son enthralled by occasional amount of dollars?

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the son is held within the other word

parts.note: fitful means irregular, happening only now and then

explanation.surface: A son captivated by the odd handful of dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the Clint Eastwood western 'A Fistful of Dollars'; the question mark flags that a fistful is only one possible quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A handful of something is as much as a hand can grasp, as in the film title about dollars.

clue.text: Steward has sorties at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naval steward makes sorties out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits a naval steward, but it signals the anagram of HAS SORTIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight attendant is an airborne steward or stewardess looking after passengers on a plane.

clue.text: Musical soirée? WI enjoy this when they're not singing?

definitions.meaning: an informal evening of improvised music by gathered players

definitions.text: WI enjoy this when they're not singing?
definitions.meaning: the Women's Institute are famous for making jam, so a jam-making session is their treat

explanation.surface: An evening of music that the Women's Institute members enjoy when not singing hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation known for jam-making and for singing 'Jerusalem' at meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of musicians playing impromptu is one sense; the other reads the phrase literally as a bout of preserve-making.

clue.text: Recall grasping fat lady?

indicators.note: recall means call back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: avid means eager or greedy, grasping

explanation.surface: Someone remembers clutching an overweight woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to 'it ain't over till the fat lady sings', the fat lady being an operatic soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna, the leading female opera singer, is jokingly the fat lady of the saying.

clue.text: Be tense during windy noises — good luck

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the tense letter sits inside

parts.note: swishes are hissing sounds like the wind makes
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Stay on edge while the wind howls outside: good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts T inside SWISHES after its first letter, giving STWISHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying good luck to someone is wishing them well, the same farewell sentiment as kind regards.

clue.text: Goddess that makes the story exciting or sinks

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the clue says it sinks, so its letters go

explanation.surface: A goddess makes a tale thrilling or else it falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinks' tells you OR disappears: rearrange THE STORY and remove OR, leaving TETHYS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Titaness was a sea deity, wife of Oceanus and mother of the river gods.

clue.text: A rugby player, very large, is well-chosen

parts.note: taken as written
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A huge rugby forward proves a fine selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite or pertinent to the situation is aptly suited, so fittingly selected.

clue.text: Case which needs objective prosecuting

definitions.meaning: the grammatical case of the direct object of a verb
bringing a charge against someone, accusing them

explanation.surface: A legal case that needs a clear aim for the prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar the objective case of English pronouns corresponds to this Latin case; the second sense is the adjective meaning accusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians name the object case so; as an adjective the word also means making an accusation.

clue.text: Supplier of clean gas concerning new airports

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: new means fresh, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A gas supplier has concerns about new airports.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing mask that filters out dust or fumes provides the wearer with purified air.

clue.text: Singular, grim chip

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
hard means harsh or grim, as in hard times

explanation.surface: A single grim chip, perhaps of broken pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment of broken glass or pottery is a chip or splinter of the material.

clue.text: Mediaeval pluckers sit with lust boiling

indicators.note: boiling means seething and churned up, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: Medieval minstrels sit seething with lust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluckers' suggests poultry workers but means players who pluck strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lute players pluck the strings of a medieval instrument, so they are plucking musicians of that era.

clue.text: Most slight English in terminal

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: last means final, terminal

explanation.surface: Very little English is spoken in the airport terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of little: smallest in amount or degree, the slightest possible.

clue.text: Go round with rapscallion

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible, untrustworthy man, a rascal

explanation.surface: Hang about with a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn or revolve in a circle, as birds or a person turning on the spot, is to rotate.

clue.text: Bread while seated in church

indicators.note: seated in means sitting inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: as means while, at the same time that

explanation.surface: Eating bread while sitting in church, perhaps at communion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, not the loaf the church setting suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is old slang for money, and ready money in notes and coins is the same thing.

clue.text: Ushered back I find some delights in this shop

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to usher is to lead, so ushered means led

explanation.surface: A shopper led back to a store full of delights.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is extended: the shop's name is itself the first half of 'delights', a bonus nod rather than separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen, shortened, is a shop selling fine foods, and its name sits within the word delights.

clue.text: Bit of toast, perhaps, cold and kind of red?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rust is a reddish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A cold, slightly burnt bit of toast.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer edge of a slice of bread, toasted or not, is one example of a hard outer layer.

clue.text: Cold cream I replaced in china cup, for example

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Cold cream is put back into a china cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Fired clay ware, such as porcelain cups and plates, is pottery, so a china cup is one example.

clue.text: After caper, old Detective Sergeant stands for cameras?

indicators.note: after means following, so the next pieces come after the first

parts.note: a caper or jaunt is a trip
DS is the police abbreviation for Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: After a prank, a veteran police sergeant poses for the cameras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands for cameras' reads as posing for photographers, but means three-legged supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-legged supports hold a camera steady, so they are stands used by photographers.

clue.text: Small, needing to get dispatched to be trained

parts.note: to dispatch is to kill

explanation.surface: A small creature must be dispatched for training.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trained in a craft has the expertise and competence that practice brings.

clue.text: Turncoat's ultimate aim?

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the final letter of the word turncoat is used

parts.note: a reason is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: What does a defector finally want?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a traitor's goal is betrayal of their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is what a defector or traitor sets out to commit.

clue.text: Behaved like invaders, possibly being cornered?

definitions.meaning: acted like the Angles, the Germanic invaders of post-Roman Britain; a whimsical verb

explanation.surface: The invaders acted as if they had been trapped in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles were a Germanic people who invaded Britain after the Romans left; 'possibly' flags that the verb is invented.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornered shape has angles; the first sense coins a verb from the Angles, the invading tribe.

clue.text: A Greek character with skill overturned shock

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so the whole string is reversed

parts.note: taken as written
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A Greek with a talent was knocked over by a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A deeply distressing experience or physical injury is a trauma, a psychological or bodily blow.

clue.text: Judge tries this jacket

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit heard before a court
a covering or casing, as for a book

explanation.surface: A judge tries on a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is tried by a judge; a protective covering such as a book's dust jacket is the second meaning.

clue.text: In favour of female head of dept at uni

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Backing a woman to head a university department.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviations 'dept' and 'uni' signal that the answer is a short form too.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor, informally shortened, typically leads an academic department at a university.

clue.text: Lawmaker improperly hosting party for US singer

indicators.note: hosting means having guests inside, so the party goes within
improperly means wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A legislator behaves badly while hosting a party for an American singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US singer' suggests a pop star but is an American songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a North American songbird of fields and grasslands, so a feathered singer.

clue.text: Instrument of heartless caustic criticism

indicators.note: heartless means having the middle removed, so the central letters go

parts.note: vitriol is bitter, caustic criticism, named after sulphuric acid

explanation.surface: An instrument of cruel, biting criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes TRI, the middle three letters of VITRIOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowed stringed instrument of the Renaissance, ancestor-cousin of the violin family.

clue.text: Tip at the east end of Derby, say, makes you disgruntled

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: Derby is an English cheese, so an example of cheese
to tip one's hat is to doff it

explanation.surface: A tip at the east end of Derby leaves you fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English city, but here it is Derby cheese; CHEESED OFF is British slang for fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for annoyed and fed up, the state of being irritated or displeased.
